notes.label: Saturation prediction
notes.value: QA: in 100 mL water, 7 complete 5 g portions should remain below the 36 g approximate capacity; 8 portions should exceed it and leave at least 4 g at equilibrium.

notes.label: Saturation observation 4
notes.value: QA: below capacity but still a positive finite-time residue. Do not call this equilibrium saturation.

notes.label: Saturation observation 5
notes.value: QA: 24 g equilibrium excess; the additional transient residue is positive but smaller than 0.000001 g.

notes.label: Saturation conclusion
notes.value: QA result: 7 complete portions (35 g) in 100 mL water left 0.011821 g transient solid with no equilibrium excess. Eight portions (40 g) left 4.002292 g solid: 4 g equilibrium excess plus 0.002292 g transient residue. C = 0.36 × 100 = 36 g; max(0,40−36) = 4 g. In fresh 200 mL water the capacity was 72 g, so 40 g had no equilibrium excess. Vessel, dose cup and supply salt summed to 60 g. Timings and rates are chosen simulation parameters; finite-time residue alone is not proof of saturation.
